subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Which parts of temp artifact provenance should become a core OpenClaw contract, and which should remain plugin or ClawHub workflow policy?
rationale: The request spans stable doctor/runtime safety, agent tool behavior, cleanup authority, and durable storage policy, while VISION.md keeps core lean and prefers plugins for optional workflow capability.

options.title: Scope Core Guardrails First
options.body: Add only generic core checks for durable state and runtime-critical temp-backed paths, and leave workflow-specific artifact classes to plugins until a missing core API is proven.

options.title: Design Core Provenance Registry
options.body: Approve a SQLite-backed temp artifact registry with explicit classes, ownership, cleanup semantics, and doctor integration as a new core product surface.

options.title: Route Mostly To ClawHub
options.body: Treat the provenance/janitor workflow as a skill or plugin package and keep core limited to existing prompt and service-path hardening.

recommendation.title: Scope Core Guardrails First
recommendation.body: Add only generic core checks for durable state and runtime-critical temp-backed paths, and leave workflow-specific artifact classes to plugins until a missing core API is proven.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the prior related scope decision and temp-path guard history, making them the best available owner for the core-versus-plugin product boundary question.
